subject: Tri-region demo — handling the clock changeover week
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@prismalabs.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Tri-region demo — handling the clock changeover week

Hi Liam —

Quick one as we're lining up the demo next week: both Redwood and Prisma Labs are affected by the US/EU daylight-saving offset this month (US springs forward on 2026-03-14, EU on 2026-03-28). That creates a two-week window where our usual "late-morning UTC" slot shifts for US vs EU attendees.

We want to avoid last-minute no-shows and ensure APAC coverage. Two practical options:

- Option A: Run two short regional sessions (US/EU) separated by 2 hours, keeping presentations identical; APAC folks can join whichever slot works or watch a 30-min recording.
- Option B: Single demo with split support: run the presentation at a time that overlaps US+EU minimally and have two hosts (one in US, one in EU) for live Q&A, plus an APAC-specific follow-up office hour.

Attached is a 1-page mutual action plan (tri-region-demo-MAP.pdf) with proposed times for both options. Can you confirm Prisma's attendee availability and whether you prefer A or B? If helpful I can also send two calendar invites (ICS) and a short run-of-show.

Proposed windows (local times):
- US-friendly: 9:00am PT / 12:00pm ET / 17:00 BST (EU) — good for US mornings, late EU afternoon.
- EU-friendly: 3:00pm BST / 10:00am PT — later EU, early US afternoon.

If you already have a preferred slot from your side, please send it over and we'll align.

Thanks —
Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Senior Account Exec, Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0199

Attachment: tri-region-demo-MAP.pdf (PDF, 1 page)

From: Liam O'Connor <liam@prismalabs.com>

Cc: Prisma Labs Sales Ops <salesops@prismalabs.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 17:23:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Tri-region demo — handling the clock changeover week

Hi Naomi —

Appreciate the heads-up. We're a little constrained on the client side: our product team in Dublin prefers late-morning local time (11:00–12:30 GMT) and our SF engineering lead can only do mornings PT (8:30–10:30 PT). APAC (Sydney) asked for an evening option but may just catch the recording.

Given that, Option B (single demo + split support) sounds better for us — keeps friction down for exec stakeholders. Two asks:

1) Can you center the main presentation around 10:30 PT / 18:30 GMT so Dublin product folks still join for Q&A, and we have the SF lead for the first half?
2) Please add a 30-minute APAC office hour the following day at 7:30 AEST; that'll work for our Sydney engineers to ask infra questions.

If that timing is tough for Redwood, we'll accept Option A (two sessions) but prefer fewer duplications.

Thanks —
Liam
Liam O'Connor
Head of Integrations, Prisma Labs
liam@prismalabs.com

Thanks Liam — Option B is doable. Quick confirmations and next steps:

- Main demo: 2026-03-18 at 10:30 PT / 18:30 GMT. We'll keep the core deck to 30 minutes + 30 minutes live Q&A.
- APAC office hour: 2026-03-19 at 7:30 AEST (30 minutes) — we'll record and circulate notes.
- Hosts: Naomi (US) + Marissa (EU). Ben will run the infrastructure deep-dive during the Q&A.

I've attached the ICS invite (naomi-demo-invite.ics) for the main demo and a short mutual-action draft. Please accept or propose a 30-min swap.

Logistics note: because the US clock moves on 2026-03-14, if any attendee is on a calendar that auto-adjusts to local DST, the invite will normalize — but for clarity we've listed the timezone string in the invite title. Please double-check calendar timezones after accepting.

If all good, Marissa and I will do a 15-minute pre-demo sync (internal) the morning of the 18th. Marissa — can you confirm availability for 2026-03-18 at 08:45 GMT?

Best,
Naomi
